evidence.claim: Iowa includes it among its state byways; Travel Iowa emphasizes the transportation history that shaped the five towns along the drive.

evidence.claim: The White Pole Auto Club created the Great White Way in 1910, following the Rock Island railroad between Council Bluffs and Des Moines.
evidence.quote: The Great White Way was formed in 1910 by the White Pole Auto Club. The route was built along the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad between Council Bluffs and Des Moines.

evidence.claim: Members painted poles white to mark the route.
evidence.quote: Members of the auto club painted poles along the route white

evidence.claim: The Great White Way Association paid five dollars to register its named trail with the Iowa State Highway Commission in 1914, becoming the first official registered route.
evidence.quote: the Great White Way Association paid the $5.00 fee (equivalent to $163.00 in 2025) to become the first official registered highway route on July 30, 1914.

evidence.claim: The later numbered highway changed again in 1980, when U.S. 6 traffic between Adair and Dexter moved onto I-80.
evidence.quote: In 1980, three lengthy sections were moved onto the Interstate: 26 miles (42 km) in western Iowa between Adair and Dexter

evidence.claim: In 2002, residents of the five towns organized to draw visitors back onto the historic road.
evidence.quote: In 2002, a group of residents from Adair, Casey, Menlo, Stuart, and Dexter formed a new group to promote the White Pole Road. Their intention was to bring visitors to their towns by diverting some traffic from the nearby I-80 / US 6 corridor to the south and onto the historic road.
